content: The truth is rarely pure and never simple.
author: Oscar Wilde
sourceWork: The Soul of Man under Socialism (1891)
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. We are conditioned to believe that more is always better—more possessions, more accomplishments, more stimulation. Yet our accumulation usually brings more anxiety, maintenance, and mental clutter.

Across his life and work, Oscar Wilde saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Wealth is not having endless things; it is wanting very little. When you realize that your deepest needs for peace, connection, and purpose cannot be bought, you become truly unshakeable.
reflectionPrompt: What creative idea or authentic voice have you held inside, and what small step can you take to express it?
